thesis: ServiceNow is fighting to be the winner rather than the victim of agentic AI: after a 14% single-day crash on Q1 2026 results (subscription revenue hit tied to the Iran war disruption) and a -9.2% June, the stock rallied on a Guggenheim upgrade ($125 target) and its 'AI Control Tower' narrative - governance/orchestration for enterprise AI agents, endorsed by Jensen Huang as 'the operating system for enterprise AI agents.' FY2026 subscription revenue guidance was still RAISED to $15.735-15.775B and Now Assist customers with $1M+ ACV are up 130% y/y. At ~$110.8B (~7x forward subscription revenue, ~66x trailing GAAP), it is the cheapest ServiceNow has been in years on sales - but SBC-heavy economics temper the cash story. Q2 results July 22 are the referendum.
catalysts: Q2 2026 results July 22, 2026 - first data point since the AI-partnership wave and the licensing reset
AI Control Tower adoption metrics; Now Assist $1M+ ACV cohort (+130% y/y)
FY2026 subscription revenue guidance $15.735-15.775B (raised) - delivery against it
Nvidia partnership/endorsement deepening ('OS for enterprise AI agents')
Guggenheim upgrade momentum (rare upgrade, $125 target July 1)
risk_factors: Agentic AI cuts both ways: if agents commoditize workflow software, ServiceNow's seat-based economics erode faster than Control Tower revenue arrives
Q1's 14% single-day crash shows how fragile the multiple is to any subscription-revenue wobble
SBC-heavy model (~15-20% of revenue historically) - per-share economics are far worse than reported FCF suggests
Weekly performance data conflicted (+15.47% snapshot vs +6.24% in coverage) - volatile, headline-driven tape
Macro/geopolitical sensitivity now demonstrated (Iran-war revenue impact management itself cited)

now_assist_momentum.unit: y/y growth ratio of $1M+ ACV customers

q1_crash.note: subscription revenue hit tied to Iran war; stock sank 14% on the print
